newsitem.title: NORWAY: Fokus and UBN discuss cooperation.
newsitem.headline: Fokus and UBN discuss cooperation.

text.p: The managements of Norway's Fokus Bank and Union Bank of Norway have had talks with the objective of establishing cooperation between the two banks, a statement said on Wednesday.
The cooperation would be based on both banks continuing as independent entities, the statement said.
The statement by the two banks said the initiative for cooperation came from Fokus Bank.

"The starting point of the talks was a shared objective regarding a nation-wide distribution network, combined with a need to utilise the banks' branch networks with a better and more complete product range," it said.

"Through binding cooperation, both banks will be able to utilise each other's distribution network and products. The two banks will continue the talks with the objective of making a long-term agreement."
Fokus Bank is Norway's fourth biggest bank and UBN, known locally as Sparebanken NOR, is the third largest. UBN is also the biggest savings bank of Norway.
The statement said Fokus, UBN and Danish insurance company Codan Forsikring had agreed on a similar cooperation in insurance. Fokus and Codan already cooperate in insurance matters in Norway.
"The cooperation between Fokus Bank and (Agrarian bank) Landkreditt will continue," it said. "The three above mentioned partners now control close to 20 percent of the shares in Fokus Bank."

UBN has cooperation agreements with five regional savings banks. When including these savings banks into the cooperation Fokus and UBN are about to enter into, it will be the most comprehensive banking group in Norway with around 425 branches and presence in every county of Norway, the statement said.
It was the latest attempt at consolidating or restructuring Norway's overbanked financial community.
A Fokus Bank spokeswoman said she believed the cooperation, if realised, would make it more difficult for Sparebankgruppen, a group of 16 savings bank, to take over Fokus.
Fokus has recommended its shareholders to turn down the hostile takeover bid by Sparebankgruppen made last month.
At the same time Fokus and Den norske Bank (DnB) have launched rival bids for mortgage lender BNbank.

Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse and insurer Storebrand meanwhile have announced plans to merge by the end of the year to form Norway's largest financial institution and the country's second largest listed company.
